key_insight: Structured EHR data enriched with medical knowledge can predict 30-day readmission nearly as well as note-based models, while staying sparse and interpretable.
clinical_relevance: This suggests hospitals may be able to build practical readmission-risk tools without relying on discharge notes, reducing compute needs and improving transparency.
method: Mapped diagnoses to a disease ontology
Grouped procedures, drugs, and lab results using medical knowledge sources
Trained six classifiers on interpretable structured features from MIMIC-IV
evidence_signal: On a MIMIC-IV v2.2 cohort with 20-fold cross-validation, the best model achieved AUROC 0.743 and performed comparably to prior structured-data and note-based approaches.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated retrospectively on one dataset, so external validation and workflow testing are needed before real-world deployment.
paper_title: Knowledge-Enriched Structured EHR Features for 30-Day Hospital Readmission Prediction on MIMIC-IV
